translations.text: An exposition he delivered one day when he saw the crowd siding with the man who deserved the curse.
He wanted them to tell him what he had repeatedly said about him, and he wanted the others to guard themselves against that man’s deeds.
God says in the scriptures that belong to him, “Children shall not die for their fathers,” and, “The fathers shall not eat sour grapes and the children’s teeth be set on edge.”
Likewise, no believing slave will die for unbelieving masters, nor will the impiety of godless masters
who worship wood and stones fall upon slaves whose hope is in God and his Christ, Jesus.
The negligence of unbelieving and oppressive masters will fall upon them, and the righteousness of believing slaves will come upon them.
There is no slavery in the place where we will go, for those who now free themselves from slavery to sin.
Since, therefore, each person will give an account of himself to God, listen to what is written: “Separate yourselves! Separate yourselves! Do not touch anything unclean!”
Do not take part in the deeds of those who are slaves of Cronus, who love and lust after Hecate, gazing at her face,
her prostitute’s appearance, lest Jesus, who hates those people, hate you along with them.
The holy scripture also said that the angels spoke with Lot, urging him to leave Sodom quickly and warning him not to perish along with them.
Now you too, O man, are being told through the word of God to separate yourself from their sins, lest he make you like them and wipe you out along with them.
There is a weakness—I lay it before whoever may encounter it—namely, that people like us, who say, “We love the one who gave us knowledge, Christ,”
accept gifts of any goods at all from godless people, or that we, in turn, take them a gift, establishing a friendship for ourselves with Christ’s enemies,
although they openly show themselves to our people, or to crowds of people, to be idolaters, worshiping images of demons and saying in their insolence,
“Just as we cannot convert you to being pagans, you cannot convert us to being Christians.”
For whoever bows down before godless people bows down before the devil who dwells in them and kisses the one they serve, the serpent.
But whoever bows down before people of God bows down before God who dwells in them and kisses the one they serve, Jesus.
If you say, “The Lord welcomes sinners and eats with them,” then consider instead the purpose: why did he do this? So that they would believe in him, or so that they would blaspheme him?
Or, if he was not going to benefit them, how could he say, “I came to call sinners to repentance”?
Or do you not see the sign of their willingness toward the one who called them? It is this: “All the tax collectors and sinners were drawing near to him to listen to him.”
If you invite an unbeliever and he comes to your God’s banquet and eats of the good things of which he said, “I have prepared them,” then that is good.
If an unbeliever invites you to a meal and you too eat with him, like your Lord Jesus, your cup is separate from that of the [?].
[?] the hands, which are far from [?].
They used to [?] certain forms that were excessively narrow or very full.
Why should I be afraid in the presence of foolish people?
And they are not ashamed to say, “There is no God.”
The lawlessness of pagans will surround me—those who trust in their wealth and boast of empty hopes.
If from the beginning they have spread evil reports about God's people, as it is written, it has also been said, “The righteous person will be remembered forever; he will not fear an evil report.”
What will the enemies of Christ say against me except the lies that come from their mouths against me, concerning all sorts of things that do not exist?
As someone said, whether rightly or wrongly, “When they speak against you in the houses of the rich, I tell them about your goodness.”
For before all the people who put their hope in Jesus, I am subject to their reproach, and their grievance is against me alone.

But those rich oppressors have nothing to say against me except, “You turn the hearts of the poor away from us, so that they will not do forced labor in the fields or at any task beyond their strength.”
And they say, “He openly entered our houses and took away the things we worship,” ashamed that they were unable to stop him.
For what other desire and what other scourge are not upon godless people, without their realizing it?
Or is this great wrath that has fallen upon them—not allowing them to know God—not enough?
But do not let any of you think, “If only God would repay those who insult us with evil!”
Instead, remember the Lord's patience: he did not make the tongues of those who cursed him fall out of their mouths.
And he did not make those who crucified him burst open in the middle, just as he has not torn out the tongues of those who blaspheme him now.
And he did not make the flesh of those who say, “He is not God,” fall off.
But they will indeed fall apart and burst open, and their tongues will split and be torn out, when the Lord Jesus shows them the day of their slaughter.
Indeed, it is laid down that God's people should pray for those who persecute them.
For this reason we bless those who curse us, in accordance with the commandment of our teacher and Lord, Christ.
For if his disciples and servants curse people on their own account, because they speak evil against them, they are blameworthy.
But if they do not curse them because they have uttered this abomination with their mouths, “The one true God alone is not God—
the Father of our Lord Jesus,” then they share in their deeds and their words.
And they share in their deeds and their words.
And they share their liability to judgment and their curse, and the wrath and Gehenna.
If, then, these people, who have gone beyond the nature of animals, have not known God or understood his signs, his mighty acts, and all his works,
not only those on earth, which they see and hear about, but also those in heaven and everything he will do—
how will they know his people and their deeds?
anyone who fears a mortal human being, a son of man—those who wither like grass—is no less ridiculous than ignorant little children who jump and tremble at
hearing the sound of foxes or seeing them.
But they cannot catch you in anything except this alone: fighting for justice and for what is right in everything.
Above all, keep yourself away from Christ’s enemies and those who oppress the poor.
For the evil words their offspring speak against us are no worse than those their father always speaks about those who oppose his thoughts.
Nor, again, are the good words that some people may speak to us better than those that Jesus, our King and our Lord, always speaks into our hearts.
Nor is the struggle against those who oppose us greater than the struggle against their father, the devil, whom we fight at all times.
If the help of brothers and friends is good when they help one another—
for it is good when people find faithful friends and true brothers—God’s help is greater than all these.
For this reason, these people and those others are not my concern.
Did not a duke, Genesius [?], a pagan duke, dare to say when he came here, “I was indeed astonished that you are happy”?
I answered him in this way: “Why would someone who has no God but Jesus not be happy?
“Do we worship handmade, demonic idols?”
As the prophets said about them: “There is no joy for the ungodly,” says the Lord God.

But woe to you, woe to you, assembly of calves and dogs and every beast in creation! God’s anger has not withdrawn from it to this day, and will remain until the end, because it is an assembly of evil people.
“An assembly of calves and dogs surrounded me,” and, “It seized me.”
The ingratitude is not hidden from Jesus, nor does he forget it, because they dishonor him and his saints within you or through them.
For they have already explained their own name: the one filled with demons, on whom every evil spirit has settled,
so that they may fulfill their desires with her, and she hers with them—the partner of those who blaspheme God.
What will you do on the day they are rebuked?
or laughing with those who laugh at you,
For they dishonor God and insult his saints while you listen.
For they do not speak insolently against God and his people in private rooms, but in marketplaces and in streets where many people hear.
I too tell you openly, in the midst of this crowd, so that the farthest reaches of the regions and the whole earth may hear:
Cursed are those who say, “God could be crucified,” or, “God dies.”
Cursed are those who say, “If God is a god, why did he not know where the devil had come from?”
They said this because they heard in Job that the King, God Almighty, asked that demon, “Where have you come from?”
They did not understand the meaning of what they heard, for God has spoken many times in the Scriptures.
For if those godless people had understood, would they not have realized that people customarily threaten [?] wicked [?] slaves and say, “Where have you come from?” even when they know?
Just as Elisha questioned Gehazi, knowing where he had come from and what he had done, so the Lord questioned the devil threateningly:
“Where are you coming from, you destroyer, you liar, you who boast over weak people?
Have you, then, you weakling, considered my servant Job? There is no one like him.
If you want to fight, turn your attention to him.
For I have put up with you, demon, to test my chosen ones, so that they may laugh at you through all those at whose hands you are put to shame when they defeat you—
you angel who is killed, you lion and dragon who is trampled by those whom I have allowed to gird themselves with strength, and whom I gird with might to oppose your godless deeds.”
Cursed are those who say, “If he is God, why did he not know where Adam was?”
For they said this because they heard in Genesis, “Adam, where are you?”
They do not know that some questions are not about hidden things, but about things that are evident and known.
It is like the way God questioned Moses, “What is this in your hand?” and Moses acknowledged, “It is a staff.”
And just as Joseph questioned his brothers, “Who are you, and where are you from?”—he was not ignorant.
For if they had understood, the kind of people who themselves said from the beginning, “How did God know?” would have shut their mouths and refrained from saying these godless things.
And, “Is there knowledge in the Most High?”
Cursed are those who say, “If Jesus is God, why did he not know where Lazarus had been laid?”
They said this because they heard in the Gospel, “Where have you laid him?”
They do not know that the Lord asked as a human being, though he is God, and that this kind of expression often occurs in speech, especially human speech.
Just as he said—or when the Lord himself did this as a human being, as it is written in Genesis, when he asked Abraham, “Where is Sarah your wife?”
Likewise, the angel asked the women at the tomb, “Whom are you looking for?”
The Lord also did this when he said to Mary, “Woman, why are you weeping? Whom are you looking for?”
Likewise, he questioned those walking to Emmaus about the things that had happened to him: “What are these things you are discussing with one another as you walk along the road?”
And just as he called to the apostles and questioned them, saying, “Children, do you have any fish?” although he knew that they had caught nothing that night.
Likewise, he also asked them, “How many loaves do you have?”
So did the one who blessed the loaves and multiplied them not know how many there were?
Or perhaps he also did not know who had touched the hem of his clothes, so that her blood stopped flowing?
Likewise, if the malice of your father Satan breaks out—or was breaking out—within you, pagan, and fills you with still more unbelief,
I will say, acknowledging the truth, that not only does he know that her blood has been flowing for twelve years, but he has known her since she was in her mother’s womb.
Even if a potter fails to recognize the vessel he made with his own hands during his lifetime, Jesus knows those whom he formed in the beginning.
Those who know that [?]

until he wiped them out because of their ungodliness, except for Lot and his children; the one who drowned Pharaoh and his multitude in the sea because of his godlessness.
Those who loved the curse, which would come upon them, said, “He cannot save himself from the hands of those who crucified him.”

The one who brought them all into being; the one who made the earth open its mouth, and it swallowed a multitude because they had sinned against him at that time, along with all those whom he wiped out in the wilderness.
The people who are even more accursed said, “If he is God, why did they crucify him?”
Who will be able to count the [?]
[?] all of them, just as a single one went out through him and killed one hundred eighty-five thousand people in a single night from the camp of the multitudes of godless people.
And Moses, his chosen one, performed all these signs in Egypt, in the Red Sea, and in the wilderness for forty years.
And all the things he did through his servant Joshua son of Nun, who was mighty in his power.
And his servant Elijah raised the dead.
And again he parted the waters of the Jordan.
He walked on dry ground.
He also shut up the sky for three years and six months.
And again he [?] fire from heaven when he called upon the name of the Most High.
It consumed the stones, the water, the wood, and the calves slaughtered upon them, which he had prepared in the form of a sacrifice.
And the ground too, which he had made like a sea, together with all the area around it.
And he prayed, and the rainwater dried up on the earth.
It yielded its fruit.
Likewise, his servant Elisha also raised the dead.
And he struck the multitude [?]
which he did in the name of the Most High.
And the accursed people said, “He is not God.”
Therefore, concerning these things, let us question the unbelievers, in whose houses God's curse rests, and not in the presence of the believers, on whose heads the Lord's blessing rests.
“Tell us, then, who is your God, O people who [?]”
If you say that those in the sky are your gods, you are cursed,
because our Lord and God—the Lord and God of us Christians—created them in the beginning to shine upon the earth.
And if you say of the calf and the cow and all the other animals that they are your gods, you are cursed, because the Lord of glory, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ,
provided them for pulling the yoke, carrying loads, eating them, drinking their milk, and clothing ourselves with their wool.
If you say that wild animals are your gods, you are even more cursed, because the Lord God commanded them all to come into being.
And if the dog and the cat are your gods, you are still more deeply cursed, because the Lord God says, “I am he, I am he, and there is no other besides me.”
He assigned them their work: the one to keep watch, and the other to catch mice.
And if wood, stones, gold, silver, bronze, iron, and all the other things you worship are your gods,
you are even more cursed, because the ruler of the whole world provided them for people, knowing that they would take them for their own use.
Do not [?] say that these godless people are cursed, as he hears words spoken by good fathers: “You must not curse anyone.”
Indeed, they are not even human beings.

But if they too are human beings, they are human beings who deserve to be cursed by those who say, “We are Christians,” because they have insulted the one who created them and slandered the one who [?] them.
If it is right to curse the serpent, it is even more right to curse the children of that serpent, whom the Lord cursed in the beginning because he deceived Eve and caused Adam to stumble in paradise.
In the same way, these cursed people now cause many to stumble, and they lead astray those who cannot understand that they belong to Satan.
Therefore, when Scripture says somewhere—or rather, when people of God say—“You must not curse anyone,” they mean, “You must not curse those who curse you,” as we have already said.
They do not mean, “You must not curse the one who insults Christ, the one who honors you.”
And if the holy ones say, speaking about the tongue, “With it we curse people,” they mean that it is foolishness for a person
to say, “I bless God,” while cursing good and faithful people against whom no one has anything to say.
This is how they said it: “My brothers, these things should not happen this way.”
And they do not mean, “You must not curse those who have bound a curse around themselves like a belt.”
And the curse entered them like water, and like oil into their bones.
When they say, “Michael the archangel, while speaking with the devil and disputing with him about the body of Moses, did not dare to bring a slanderous judgment against him,”
do not think they mean, “You must not curse people who sacrifice to demons,”
as I heard some of you say: “Michael certainly did not speak harsh words to the devil at all.”
But he said, “May the Lord rebuke you.” “This is how it is,” they said: “We should not curse people who cast images of Cronus.”
But this is not what the statement means: that the great archangel showed respect for that devil by not cursing him.
This statement, [?] now, “May the Lord rebuke you,” signifies all the more the curse that is coming upon him.
I will not hesitate to say that he is cursed, along with his pagan children.
He is all the more cursed along with them.
They are cursed along with him.
Or do you not see that this is not so?
What, then, does a curse have to do with a slanderous judgment?
Quite apart from what the Scriptures have said, whenever ignorant, fruitless, and impure people read at all,
they say things they do not understand, like these accursed people now, who apply them to blaspheming the greatness of God, because they know neither him nor his works.
Listen now, so that we may understand that we alter the words the saints wrote, applying them to our own desires in this way. Is it not because we do not want sound teaching?
And so that we may understand that they are speaking about people whom they compared to empty clouds driven along by the wind,
and to dry, fruitless trees that have died a second time in their roots, and to violent waves of the sea that bring forth their shame,
and to stars that have gone astray, for whom thick darkness has been prepared forever, because they dare to say things that are improper and things they do not understand.
You see that they find no fault with those who pour curses down upon those who disbelieve everything written in the Scriptures:
the things that the Lord God did, and those that his saints did in his name.
So it now says about them, “Likewise, these people, dreaming, defile the flesh, reject authority, and blaspheme glorious beings.”
They rebuke the offspring of the ungodly at all times, right down to these accursed people now, because they blaspheme things they do not understand.
But in the things they understand, as animals do, they destroy themselves.
God of hosts, the Almighty, whose glory, wonders, and good things have filled the whole inhabited world—
they reject him and blaspheme him.
But the crooked devil, whose wonders have filled the whole earth—these accursed people are his slaves.
Through him they destroy themselves in every kind of lawlessness.
The house of God, the church, which shines upon the whole earth, is filled with words of life.
But their houses, which have become lodgings for
demons and are filled with deceptive books and every deceitful practice—in these they destroy themselves.
But I return once more to say that it is not Satan alone against whom the great archangel Michael brings a slanderous judgment, but also those who, through him, fell away from the straight path.
They also said, “The angels did not bring a slanderous judgment against them,” just as they also wrote about the people who turned aside and became worthless,
and went after flesh because they despised authority, being audacious and self-willed.
They do not tremble before the glory, speaking abusively of the place where the angels are greater in power and strength, yet do not bring an abusive judgment against them.
But these people were born like animals governed by instinct, for capture and destruction, speaking abusively about things they do not understand.
They will perish in their destruction, ending in ruin, receiving the wages of wrongdoing. They consider their daytime indulgence a pleasure.
They are brazen and filthy, living luxuriously and delighting in their deceptions, their eyes full of adultery.
They do not stop sinning. They deceive those who are not firmly established, having trained themselves—or their hearts—in acts of exploitation. They are children of the curse.
I said again: Stop cursing those who have perished because of their foolishness. Stop bringing an abusive judgment against them, or speaking abusively.
Therefore, when they say that Michael the archangel did not bring an abusive judgment against them,
and that the angels do not bring an abusive judgment against these others, they are not sparing Satan and those who followed them.
Who among those able to kill a dragon that has killed many with its venom would spare it?
Rather, the person who uttered it understands it correctly.
Now this expression, “an abusive judgment,” which he did not dare to bring against the devil,
or against the others who do his evil deeds, conveys a meaning like this: He did not dare to say, “If only the Lord God had never brought him into existence at all,
if you were destined to change in this way through your apostasy and become a devil!
And if only he had not brought into existence the people who chose to have the hearts of animals—the pagans, the barbarians, and every godless heretic!
If only he would destroy you and his angels before the appointed time, pouring out all his anger upon you
and bringing the full force of his wrath upon those who loved your alien voice and followed you,
rather than listening to the voice of the one who came into the world to rescue them, Jesus, and to save them from their godlessness.”
This is the abusive judgment that absolutely none of the children of God, from angels to human beings, will dare to utter.
For this sort of thinking belongs to grumbling people who find fault with God without cause, although everything he created is good,
even if they have changed and become corrupt by their own choice.
They did not dare to bring an abusive judgment against them, as the pagans and heretics now do, daring to utter things they should not.

What did the God-loving count Chosroes say—the man whose resolve to come to us you could not break?
He said, giving glory to God, “You have made the desert a city.”
They themselves said it differently in Panopolis, twisting the statement and telling lies.

for it is good when a person finds faithful friends and true brothers—yet God's help is greater than all these.

I answered him this way: “Why should those who have no God except Jesus not rejoice?

Or will you laugh at yourself?
For they insult God and revile his saints. Listen!
They speak abusively against God and his people, not in private rooms but in marketplaces and broad streets, where many people hear.
I too say it openly in the midst of this crowd, so that [?] the districts and the whole land may hear:
Cursed are those who say, “God can be crucified,” or, “God can die.”
Cursed are those who say, “If God is God, why did he not know where the devil had come from?”
They said this because they heard in Job the King, the Lord God Almighty, asking that demon, saying, “[?]”
Speaking like a human being in the Scriptures.
For if those godless people had understood that it is human custom to threaten wicked slaves and say, “Where are you coming from?” even when they know,
just as Elisha questioned Gehazi, knowing where he had come from and what he had done, so the Lord questioned the devil threateningly:
“Where are you coming from, you destroyer, you who boast over crooked people?
Have you then paid attention, you weakling, to my servant Job? There is no one like him.
If you want to fight, go against this man.

For I have tolerated you, demon, as a test for my chosen ones, so that they may laugh at you through all the things you demand from them, as they defeat you—you angel who is killed by those who ask for [?]
